resolutions.reasoning: Mainline stable fixes the LVDS selector parent names to reference the correctly registered MIPI/LVDS bypass clocks. NXP's side only kept the older lvds0/lvds1 bypass names and a formatting style difference on the lvds1 declaration. I applied the stable clock-name fix for both LVDS selectors while preserving NXP's declaration formatting for lvds1.

NXP vendor used the old LVDS bypass clock name "lvds1_bypass_clk" while mainline stable changes it to "mipi1_lvds_bypass_clk" as part of the LVDS bypass/pixel/phy clock fix. This is a direct stable bug fix and there is only one parent slot, so the corrected mainline clock name should replace the old vendor name.

Both sides register the same LVDS0 bypass, pixel, and phy clocks with the same SCU resources and clock IDs; the only difference is the clock names. Mainline stable intentionally renames them to mipi0_lvds_* as the LVDS clock fix, while the NXP side has the older lvds0_* names and does not add independent functionality. Applied the stable fix rather than duplicating the same hardware clocks under two names.

NXP kept the existing lvds1_* clock names, while stable renamed the same LVDS_1 bypass/pixel/phy clock registrations to mipi1_lvds_* as part of the LVDS clock fix. The names are externally visible clock identifiers, so I preserved the NXP names and also added the stable fixed names for the same SCU resources.

NXP added the CONFIG_AHCI_IMX sg_io_buffer_hack declaration/NULL fallback and retained a comment documenting the locking requirement. Mainline changed scsi_eh_wakeup() to accept a precomputed busy count. These changes are independent, so both are preserved: keep the NXP sg_io_buffer_hack block and comment, and use the mainline function signature with the busy parameter.
